title: PRUSSIC. II. ALMA imaging of dense-gas tracers in SDP.81: Evidence for low mechanical heating and a sub-solar metallicity in a z = 3.04 dusty galaxy
question: What are the dense-gas properties, relative contribution of mechanical heating, and gas-phase metallicity in the z=3.042 gravitationally lensed dusty star-forming galaxy SDP.81?

data.angular_resolution: 0.36x0.24 arcsec (2016.1.00663.S), 0.33x0.29 arcsec (2018.1.00747.S), 2.3x2.1 arcsec (2017.1.01694.S); spatial scales 0.29 to 46 arcsec for HCN/HCO+, 2.1 to 46 arcsec for HNC

what.value: J_upp=1 HCN(1-0), HCO+(1-0), and HNC(1-0) upper limits in SDP.81

evidence.quote: | $J_\mathrm{upp}=1$ lines (cite: Rybak2022a) |
| $L{'}^\mathrm{sky}_\mathrm{HCN(1-0)}$ | [K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$] | $\leq3.7\times10^{10}$ |

what.value: CO(1-0) luminosity and FWHM in SDP.81

evidence.quote: : Global properties of SDP.81. Individual columns list the source position, source and lens redshift ($z_L$, $z_L$), sky-plane (observed) FIR and CO(1–0) luminosities, CO(1–0) FWHM (cite: Valtchanov2011), and FIR continuum magnification (cite: Rybak2020b).

what.value: FIR luminosity, FIR continuum magnification (mu_160um = 18.2 +- 1.2), CO(5-4) and CO(8-7) constraints, and 200-pc resolution PDR G and n parameter space

evidence.quote: : Global properties of SDP.81. Individual columns list the source position, source and lens redshift ($z_L$, $z_L$), sky-plane (observed) FIR and CO(1–0) luminosities, CO(1–0) FWHM (cite: Valtchanov2011), and FIR continuum magnification (cite: Rybak2020b).
If we restrict the parameter space to the $G$, $n$ range from the 200-pc resolution PDR modelling from (cite: Rybak2020b), only models with low mechanical heating ($\alpha$=0–10%) are left.

what.value: HCN ladder excitation conversion factors from nearby galaxies compilation

evidence.quote: For a better comparison, we converted the $J_\mathrm{upp}\geq2$ luminosities using the HCN ladder from the compilation of (cite: Israel2023); the corresponding mean line ratios are$L'_\mathrm{HCN(3-2)}/L'_\mathrm{HCN(1-0)}=0.322$, $L'_\mathrm{HCN(4-3)}/L'_\mathrm{HCN(1-0)}=0.128$.

what.value: Radiative transfer predictions for HCN(5-4)/HCN(1-0) = 0.094 in Milky Way central molecular zone

evidence.quote: The HCN(5–4) line is not included in the (cite: Israel2023) data; following (cite: Bethermin2018), we use radiative transfer predictions for the Milky Way’s central molecular zone from (cite: Mills2013) to set $L'_\mathrm{HCN(5-4)}/L'_\mathrm{HCN(1-0)}=0.094$.

what.value: z=0 HCN(4-3) and HCO+(4-3) galaxy measurements and L_FIR - L' correlations

evidence.quote: Figure 3 puts our HCN(4–3) and HCO$^+$(4–3) measurements in the context of $z=0$ studies (cite: Zhang2014; Tan2018) and the predicted $L_\mathrm{FIR}-L'$ relations from (cite: Zhang2014).

recipe.goal: Calibrate, concatenate, and re-weight multi-epoch ALMA Band 3 visibilities
recipe.method: Reduce data with standard ALMA pipeline, exclude unusable 2021 data from 2018.1.00747.S, concatenate datasets, and recalculate visibility weights consistently using statwt.

recipe.goal: Image Band 3 continuum and subtract continuum from visibilities
recipe.method: Image continuum using line-free channels in tclean with a manual mask down to 1.5 sigma; subtract continuum in uv-plane using uvcontsub with a constant flux fit.
assumptions: Constant continuum flux across the spectrum for uvcontsub

recipe.goal: Create dirty spectral cubes and narrow-band (moment-0) images of HCN(4-3), HCO+(4-3), and HNC(4-3)
recipe.method: Produce dirty images without deconvolution using tclean, applying uv-taper to HCN(4-3) and HCO+(4-3) to suppress sidelobes from discrepant array configurations, and make narrow-band (moment-0) images over a 430 km/s bandwidth.
key_parameters: final tapered beam FWHM ~ 0.85'' x 0.94'' for HCN(4-3) and HCO+(4-3)
assumptions: Line width equals CO(3-2) FWHM of 430 km/s

recipe.goal: Extract line fluxes, upper limits, and sky-plane line luminosities
recipe.method: Extract flux from a manually drawn aperture over the main lens arc (~6 beams for HCN and HCO+, 1.5 beams for HNC), adopt 3 sigma upper limits for undetected HCN and HNC, and multiply fluxes by 1.31 to account for total line flux vs flux within FWHM.
key_parameters: aperture area ~ 6 beams (HCN, HCO+) and 1.5 beams (HNC)
assumptions: Flat LambdaCDM cosmology with Omega_m=0.315 and H_0=67.4 km s^-1 Mpc^-1
Contribution from the counterimage is negligible; differential magnification between HCN and HCO+ is limited (<= 15%)

recipe.goal: Constrain mechanical heating and gas-phase metallicity via PDR modelling
recipe.method: Compare observed dense-gas line luminosity ratios (HCO+(4-3)/HCN(4-3), HCO+(4-3)/HNC(4-3), HCO+(4-3)/HCN(1-0)) and CO(5-4) (plus optionally CO(8-7) and 200-pc G, n constraints) against the Kazandjian et al. (2012, 2015) PDR model grid across metallicity Z = 0.1 to 2.0 Z_odot and mechanical heating alpha.
assumptions: Semi-infinite parallel-plane slab morphology illuminated by external UV radiation, X-ray and CR contributions; Salpeter stellar IMF; mechanical heating due to supernovae shock dissipation only (Loenen et al. 2008 prescription) injected uniformly; all radiation due to star formation (no AGN); solar metallicity 12+log(O/H)=8.69 (Asplund et al. 2009)

recipe.goal: Characterise foreground CO(0-1) absorption and companion galaxy CO(1-0) emission
recipe.method: Identify foreground absorption feature at 87.9 GHz and companion emission line at 88.62 GHz, compare companion with VLT-MUSE optical imaging/spectroscopy, fit Gaussian profile using CASA imfit, and derive CO luminosity and molecular gas mass.
assumptions: Milky-Way CO-to-H2 conversion factor alpha_CO = 4.3 M_odot/(K km s^-1 pc^2) including helium

evidence.quote: | $S^{\mathrm{sky}}_\mathrm{3\mathrm{mm}}$ | [mJy] | 0.510$\pm$0.031 |
| $S\Delta v_\mathrm{HCN(4-3)}$ | [Jy km s$^{-1}$] | $\leq$0.302 |
| $S\Delta v_\mathrm{HNC(4-3)}$ | [Jy km s$^{-1}$] | $\leq$0.207 |
| $L{'}^\mathrm{sky}_\mathrm{HCN(4-3)}$ | [K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{2}$] | $\leq7.2\times10^9$ |
| $L{'}^\mathrm{sky}_\mathrm{HNC(4-3)}$ | [K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{2}$] | $\leq7.1\times10^9$ |
As shown in Fig. 5, the slightly overluminous HCO$^+$(4–3) line and the upper limit on HCN(4–3) combine to a HCO$^+$(4–3)/HCN(4–3) ratio of $\geq$2.2.

For the comparison with models, we used the following dense-gas line ratios: $L'_\mathrm{HCO^+(4-3)}$/$L'_\mathrm{HCN(4-3)}\geq2.2$, $L'_\mathrm{HCO^+(4-3)}$/$L'_\mathrm{HNC(4-3)}\geq2.3$, and $L'_\mathrm{HCO^+(4-3)}$/$L'_\mathrm{HCN(1-0)}\geq3.8$ (see Table 1).
The $L'_\mathrm{HCO^+(4-3)}/L'_\mathrm{HCO^+(1-0)}$ ratio is $\geq$0.38, that is, consistent with a sub-thermal excitation.

For the comparison with models, we used the following dense-gas line ratios: $L'_\mathrm{HCO^+(4-3)}$/$L'_\mathrm{HCN(4-3)}\geq2.2$, $L'_\mathrm{HCO^+(4-3)}$/$L'_\mathrm{HNC(4-3)}\geq2.3$, and $L'_\mathrm{HCO^+(4-3)}$/$L'_\mathrm{HCN(1-0)}\geq3.8$ (see Table 1).
Our PDR modelling also indicates that SDP.81 has a sub-solar metallicity ($Z=0.5$ $Z_\odot$).
If we restrict the parameter space to the $G$, $n$ range from the 200-pc resolution PDR modelling from (cite: Rybak2020b), only models with low mechanical heating ($\alpha$=0–10%) are left.
When we repeated our analysis including the CO(8–7) line (which is concentrated in the northern part of the source), the only feasible models are $Z=0.5$ $Z_\odot$ and $\alpha=0-5$%.

answer_key.quantity: Foreground absorption feature flux at 87.9 GHz

evidence.loc: CO(0–1) absorption from the foreground galaxy
evidence.quote: In addition, the emission from the SDP.81 itself, we find a pronounced negative feature around 87.9 GHz, with a total flux of 0.41$\pm$0.05 Jy km s$^{-1}$ (Fig. 2).

answer_key.quantity: Foreground companion galaxy CO(1-0) line flux

evidence.loc: A serendipitous discovery of CO(1–0) emission from a companion of the SDP.81 lensing galaxy
evidence.quote: The line is centred at 88.62 GHz, a total line flux of 0.9 Jy km s$^{-1}$ and with a FWZI width of 210 km s$^{-1}$ (Fig. 9).

evidence.loc: A serendipitous discovery of CO(1–0) emission from a companion of the SDP.81 lensing galaxy
evidence.quote: We estimate the CO(1–0) luminosity as $L_\mathrm{CO(1-0)}=2\times10^6$ $L_\odot$, $L'_\mathrm{CO(1-0)}=4.5\times10^9$ K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{2}$.

answer_key.quantity: Foreground companion galaxy molecular gas mass (M_gas)

evidence.loc: A serendipitous discovery of CO(1–0) emission from a companion of the SDP.81 lensing galaxy
evidence.quote: Therefore, we hypothesise that this is a gas-rich counterpart to the lensing elliptical galaxy, with $M_\mathrm{gas}\simeq2\times10^{10}$ $M_\odot$ (assuming a Milky-Way CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor $\alpha_\mathrm{CO}=4.3$ $M_\odot$/(K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$), (cite: Bolatto2013), and including the contribution of helium).

answer_key.quantity: Foreground companion galaxy CO(1-0) Gaussian source size

evidence.loc: A serendipitous discovery of CO(1–0) emission from a companion of the SDP.81 lensing galaxy
evidence.quote: Fitting a Gaussian profile to the observed emission using the `imfit` task yields a source size of $\approx$ 3.9" $\times$ 2.8".

score_reason: The ALMA project codes, excluded execution blocks,CASA tasks, line-free frequency ranges, velocity integration widths, and flux correction factors are clearly stated. Minor deductions for unstated tclean weighting, exact uv-taper values, manual aperture coordinates, and non-public PDR model grid tables.
rediscovery_reason: All three ALMA datasets are public in the archive, the imaging recipe (dirty moment-0 maps over a 430 km/s window with uvcontsub and tapering to ~0.85x0.94 arcsec) is straightforward to replicate, and the primary results are clear numeric fluxes and luminosity ratios.
